# 100 Dials

> AI cold-call training for SDR teams. Reps dial a realistic AI prospect built from their own targets at three levels of difficulty; every call ends with the prospect's decision and a transcript, and a scored coach's review is one click away. Managers see skills by rep, the objections the team mishandles, a team leaderboard and a Monday digest.

## Pages

- [Homepage](https://100dials.com/): what it does, how it works, the three levels
- [For sales managers](https://100dials.com/for-managers): ramp, visibility, team stats, momentum
- [For sales enablement](https://100dials.com/for-enablement): grounding in real transcripts, one rubric, measurement
- [Pricing](https://100dials.com/pricing): per-seat plans and the free trial
- [Refer a sales team](https://100dials.com/refer): the referral programme, a month free for the referrer and 20% off for the referred team, plus calls earned for posts and invited reps
- [The research behind 100 Dials](https://100dials.com/research): nine studies on simulation, practice and feedback, what they show and don't, how the product uses each
- [Trust and security](https://100dials.com/trust): data handling, retention, deletion
- [Company](https://100dials.com/company): who makes 100 Dials, where it is hosted, pricing and contact in one place
- [Blog](https://100dials.com/blog): research-backed guides on cold calling
- [Practice cold calls free: can you survive Karen?](https://100dials.com/karen): a free three-minute cold call against our rudest AI prospect, work email only, scored report after
- [Objection library](https://100dials.com/objections): fifteen cold-call objections, each with what it means, three ways to handle it and a worked exchange

## Facts

- Free trial: 10 calls over 14 days, work email required, no card.
- Pricing per seat per month: Starter $79 / €75 (40 calls), Team $159 / €149 (100 calls); 20% off annual. Charged in EUR or USD, VAT excluded. 30-day money-back guarantee on the first payment.
- Scoring rubric: opener, reason for call, discovery, objection handling, value proposition, close.
- Knowledge sources that ground the prospects: 10 on trial, 30 on Starter, 100 on Team. Call recordings, transcripts and replay on every plan.
- Objection taxonomy: sixteen types tagged on every reviewed call with how the rep handled them.
- Customer data is never used to train models.

## Recent posts

- [Cold calling statistics 2026: 50 figures with their sources](https://100dials.com/blog/cold-calling-statistics): fifty figures from Gong, Cognism, Bridge Group, Orum, RAIN Group and Gartner with their sources, and eight famous statistics that have none
- [Hyperbound vs Second Nature vs 100 Dials: price, fit, grounding](https://100dials.com/blog/hyperbound-vs-second-nature-vs-100-dials): what each is built for, how each is priced, and who should pick which, checked October 2026
- [AI sales roleplay software pricing: who publishes a price](https://100dials.com/blog/ai-sales-roleplay-software-pricing): seven vendors in one table, what the quote-only tiers are called, and how to compare a seat price with a quote
- [Hyperbound alternatives: five tools, sorted by how you buy them](https://100dials.com/blog/hyperbound-alternatives): five alternatives sorted by whether you can see a price and start today, with where Hyperbound still wins
- [Second Nature alternatives for teams that cannot wait for a demo](https://100dials.com/blog/second-nature-alternatives): alternatives by reason for leaving, two with a published price and a trial
- [Nooks AI roleplay alternative: practice without buying a dialler](https://100dials.com/blog/nooks-ai-roleplay-alternative): what Nooks and Orum offer for roleplay inside a dialler, when that is right, and what to check in a standalone tool
- [Practice cold calling without real prospects: a 4-week plan](https://100dials.com/blog/practice-cold-calling-without-real-prospects): the three ways to practise without a live list, a week-by-week drill plan with calls per day and level, and the numbers that say a rep is ready
- [Cold call practice for beginners: the first ten calls](https://100dials.com/blog/cold-call-practice-for-beginners): drill the opener, the reason for call and one objection, ignore discovery and the pitch for now, three opening mistakes, and a 0 to 10 self-check table
- [Sales roleplay examples: six cold call scenarios, scripted](https://100dials.com/blog/sales-roleplay-examples): one two-minute scenario per rubric skill with a prospect brief, sample lines and a pass condition, plus a summary table
- [Cold call simulator: the practice tool roleplay cannot replace](https://100dials.com/blog/cold-call-simulator): peer roleplay, recorded-call review and AI simulators compared, what each is for, and a weekly shape that runs all three
- [Average SDR ramp time: three months, and where the weeks go](https://100dials.com/blog/average-sdr-ramp-time): three definitions of ramp, where the weeks go, how it changes with team size, and the part you can cut
- [Cold call scorecard template: six skills and how to weight them](https://100dials.com/blog/cold-call-scorecard-template): the six skills, the weights, and a 0 to 10 anchor per skill so two managers agree
- [AI cold call practice software: what to look for, what to ignore](https://100dials.com/blog/ai-cold-call-practice-software): the four things that decide whether reps improve, and the features to ignore
- [The best and worst cold call openers, from 300 million calls](https://100dials.com/blog/best-cold-call-openers): the best cold call openers sound familiar or ask permission, then state the reason for the call. The worst asks if it is a bad time. Gong's rate for each.
- [How much should an SDR talk on a cold call?](https://100dials.com/blog/cold-call-talk-ratio): on a cold call the rep talks slightly more than half the time, not the 30 percent used for discovery. The longest monologue matters more than the ratio.
- [How to handle "just send me an email" without sending the email](https://100dials.com/blog/handling-send-me-an-email): agree in two words, ask what the email would have to answer, answer that in one sentence, then ask for fifteen minutes at a set time. The exact words.
- [The reason for the call: the 15 seconds that decide a cold call](https://100dials.com/blog/reason-for-call): stating why you are calling, specifically and early, is the most reliable move on a cold call. How to build the line, five examples, and what to avoid.
- [How to run cold call roleplay that reps do not hate](https://100dials.com/blog/cold-call-roleplay): cold call roleplay works when there is no audience, one skill per session, a prospect who can say no and one rubric. A weekly format and how to score it.
- [The eight cold call objections you hear most, and what to say](https://100dials.com/blog/common-cold-call-objections): the eight objections that end most cold calls, what each usually means, and a one-line response for each that acknowledges, isolates and redirects.
- [A 30-60-90 day SDR onboarding plan that gets to booked meetings](https://100dials.com/blog/sdr-onboarding-plan-30-60-90): a 30-60-90 day SDR onboarding plan: practice before real dials, live dials with daily review, then a target, and the number that says each phase is done.
